problems.title: Robotics club team
problems.statement: A robotics club has {{J}} juniors and {{S}} seniors. In how many ways can a team of {{j}} juniors and {{s}} seniors be chosen?

common_wrong.feedback: That counts ordered picks. A team has no order: the same {{j}} juniors picked in a different order is the same team.
Adding counts teams of only juniors or only seniors. Every team has both, so each junior group pairs with every senior group.
That counts every team of {{j}}+{{s}} people, including ones with the wrong mix of juniors and seniors.

slot_mistakes.feedback: That's everyone in the club. This part only picks from the juniors.
That's everyone in the club. This part only picks from the seniors.

help_steps.title: Choose the juniors
help_steps.text: Pick $j$ of the $J$ juniors. Order doesn't matter in a team.

help_steps.title: Choose the seniors
help_steps.text: Pick $s$ of the $S$ seniors the same way.

help_steps.title: Both happen, so multiply
help_steps.text: Every group of juniors goes with every group of seniors. Now fill in the numbers.

solution.title: Pick the juniors
solution.explanation: Order doesn't matter on a team, so choosing {{j}} of {{J}} juniors is an unordered choice.

solution.title: Pick the seniors
solution.explanation: The same reasoning for the seniors: {{s}} of {{S}}.

solution.title: Combine the two counts
solution.explanation: Every team has both juniors and seniors, and the two choices don't affect each other, so multiply (the product rule).

problems.title: Robotics club team with a captain
problems.statement: A robotics club has {{J}} juniors and {{S}} seniors. A team of {{j}} juniors and {{s}} seniors is chosen, and one of the juniors on the team is named captain. How many different teams with a captain are possible?

answer.prompt: Total number of teams with a captain

common_wrong.feedback: That counts the teams but not the captain. Each team can have any of its {{j}} juniors as captain.
The captain has to be one of the {{j}} juniors on the team, not any of the {{J}} juniors in the club.

slot_mistakes.feedback: The captain comes from the juniors already on the team, not the whole club.

help_steps.title: Pick the captain from them
help_steps.text: Any of the $j$ chosen juniors can be captain: $j$ ways.

help_steps.title: Choose the seniors and multiply
help_steps.text: Pick $s$ of the $S$ seniors. All three choices happen, so multiply. Now fill in the numbers.

solution.title: Pick the juniors
solution.explanation: An unordered choice of {{j}} of the {{J}} juniors.

solution.title: Name a captain
solution.explanation: Any of the {{j}} juniors on the team can be captain.

solution.title: Pick the seniors
solution.explanation: An unordered choice of {{s}} of the {{S}} seniors.

solution.title: Combine
solution.explanation: All three choices happen together, so multiply.
